A place in the League Cup third round is at stake as Tottenham host Charlton in a London derby at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. The last competitive meeting between these sides came in the FA Cup back in January 2011, with Tottenham winning that game 3-0 at White Hart Lane. A then 19-year-old Andros Townsend made his debut that day and scored, with Jermain Defoe scoring a brace.

Tottenham’s Premier League campaign got off to the worst possible start as they lost 3-0 at Brentford last weekend. Tottenham have been very busy during this summer transfer window and that has continued this week. Savio (formerly Savinho) has arrived from Manchester City in a deal that could be worth £85m and the Brazilian could make his Tottenham debut tonight, having been registered in time.

“I think in attacking positions we need players capable one-on one, to create something, to create a chance to score,” Roberto De Zerbi said. “In terms of one-on-one, he [Savio] is one of the best players, especially since 2024. He can play on the right side, on the left side. I have known him from a long time, I spoke with him when he went to Manchester City. He is a big player for us.

“I do not know if I am the right man [to get the most out of Savio], but for sure he has to achieve. I think a player who is so good in one-on-one, so good at creating chances to score, to be complete, he has to score. If you analyse the other best wingers in the world, many of them, they score 10 to 15 goals per season. He has the qualities. Maybe his habits, he has to change habits, because he has to be focused on the assists, the one-on-one dribbling and also to score.”

Omar Marmoush is closing in on an initial loan deal from Manchester City but that move is not complete and thus he is not available for Tottenham tonight. Micky van der Ven and Pedro Porro are both available having missed Tottenham’s loss at Brentford but the hosts are still without Xavi Simons, Pape Sarr, Dejan Kulusevski and Wilson Odobert.

Charlton have made the perfect start to their Championship campaign; a 2-1 home win over Derby was followed up by a 2-1 victory at recently-relegated West Ham. Nathan Jones’ side earned their place in the League Cup second round with a 3-1 win at Cheltenham in the first round.

“We have to be very organised and very professional, they [Tottenham] are a top team,” Jones said. “They have a great manager and a brilliant group of players. They already had a Premier League squad and they have spent, what is reaching about, I do not know, £300 million or something like that. It is a wonderful test, we have to be right near our best and do both sides of the game very well. Of course, you want to test yourself against the best managers and you want to test yourself against the best teams. For us, this is not our priority, the Championship is our priority, but this is the next game and therefore it is the most important.”

#1831. Crewe Alexandra vs Wigan Athletic - prediction, team news, lineups

By Calum Burrowes | 09 Nov 2026 09:50, Last updated: 10 Nov 2026 09:53

Wigan Athletic travel to Gresty Road on Tuesday night to face Crewe Alexandra in their third and final EFL Trophy group-stage fixture.

The hosts can still secure qualification for the knockout stages but need to pick up at least a point, while the Latics head into the midweek encounter top of Northern Group B and firmly in control of their own destiny.

Having been relegated from League One at the end of the 2021-22 season, Crewe Alexandra have spent the past five campaigns in the fourth tier, where they are hoping to mount a serious promotion challenge after making a promising start to the 2026-27 season.

After falling away from the playoff race with three defeats and a draw in their final four matches last season to finish 11 points short of seventh, Crewe have made a much stronger start this time around and sit in the League Two top four after 14 matches.

Led by Lee Bell, who celebrated his fourth anniversary in charge last week, Crewe have won five, drawn seven and lost two of their opening 14 league matches to collect 22 points.

However, defeats to Exeter City and Chesterfield, along with a home draw against Barnet, have allowed leaders Salford City to open up a nine-point advantage.

Bell's side successfully carried their early-season momentum into their EFL Trophy campaign, thrashing Aston Villa Under-21s 4-1 in their opening group fixture thanks to goals from Luke Offord, Adrien Thibaut and a brace from Jack Lankester.

Despite drawing with Blackpool in normal time before losing on penalties at the start of October, the Railwaymen have collected four points from their opening two matches and need a positive result on Tuesday to reach the knockout stages for the third consecutive season.

As for Wigan Athletic, they head into their second cup fixture in the space of four days after booking their place in the second round of the FA Cup with a 3-0 victory over Boreham Wood.

Demonstrating their pedigree in the competition, which they famously won in 2013, the Latics swept aside their National League opponents to claim their first away victory of the campaign, with an early strike from Jon Mellish followed by a brace from defender Morgan Fox.

It has been a difficult start to the 2026-27 season for Gary Caldwell and his side, who currently sit in the League One relegation zone after recording three wins, two draws and nine defeats from their opening 14 matches.

Although no side in the third tier has suffered more defeats than Wigan, they travel to Cheshire on the back of their best run of form so far this season, with Saturday's FA Cup success following a victory over Bromley and a home draw against Mansfield Town.

Having collected maximum points from their opening two group matches, the Latics can still progress to the knockout stages even if they lose on Tuesday, marking a significant improvement on last season when they finished bottom of Northern Group A.

Having both secured victories in the FA Cup at the weekend, Crewe and Wigan are expected to make several changes for their return to EFL Trophy action.

Crewe have recently brought James Jones back to the club on a short-term deal until the New Year, and although he was an unused substitute in their FA Cup win over Wimbledon, he could be in contention to start on Tuesday.

Lankester has scored twice in two EFL Trophy appearances this season but has not featured since the second group fixture more than a month ago, and he is expected to remain unavailable for this encounter.

Wigan, meanwhile, will once again be without Scott Hogan, who missed Saturday's trip to Boreham Wood after being forced off during the first half of their previous match against Mansfield Town.

Dara Costelloe is also set to remain on the sidelines, with a groin injury expected to keep him out for the next four weeks.

James Carragher is expected to retain his place at the centre of a back three alongside Finley Burns and Welsh defender Fox, who will be full of confidence after scoring twice in the FA Cup victory.

Crewe Alexandra possible starting lineup:

Booth; Dancey, Offord, Graves, Ure; Moore, White; Ewusi, Thibaut, Gibson; McNeill

Walsh; Burns, Carragher, Fox; Barrett, Weir, Power, A. Harris; Burrowes, Saydee, Mellish

With Wigan arriving in their best form of the season and boasting the advantage of playing a division above their hosts, we expect Caldwell's side to complete the group stage with a third successive victory.

Although a win would represent only their second away success of the campaign, the Latics should have enough quality to demonstrate their superiority over a side competing in the fourth tier.

#1829. Liverpool: Trey Nyoni impact under Andoni Iraola cannot be ignored

By Axel Clody | 09 Nov 2026 09:57

In a transfer market that moves as many millions as the Premier League’s, where all 20 clubs are looking to invest in signings that can raise the level of their squads, the answer is often already within the club. One such case is Liverpool’s.

Trey Nyoni’s performances so far, a midfielder of just 19, show that the youngster could be the solution for the starting XI until the end of the season. With maturity above the average, the Englishman shows excellent vision, courage on the ball and quality in building play.

Against Arsenal earlier this month, in the Premier League, he led the match in accurate passes (53), pass accuracy (96%) and line-breaking passes (14), according to Opta data.

Against Fenerbahce last Wednesday, he then scored his first goal for Liverpool in a secure performance in midfield. The numbers with and without the ball also caught the eye.

Accurate passes: 89/96 (93%) Passes in the opposition half: 58/64 (91%) Passes in own half: 31/32 (97%) Long balls: 4/5 (80%) Tackles: 2/2 Interceptions: 3 Ball recoveries: 9 Ground duels: 2/4 Blocked shots: 1

In a midfield that is falling short, Nyoni is the positive news that could change Liverpool’s outlook.

That was Nyoni’s 12th game for Liverpool at the start of this season, half of them as a starter. The youngster was discovered in 2023, when he stood out for Leicester City’s Under-18s at just 15 years old.

His prominence in Liverpool’s youth system soon caught the attention of then manager Jurgen Klopp. At 16, he made his debut for Liverpool at Anfield, in an FA Cup match. Before the youngster replaced Harvey Elliott, Klopp and Nyoni looked at each other and smiled together, perhaps both already knowing the future in store for the gem.

In the last transfer window, Liverpool turned down a £30m proposal from Nottingham Forest because they believe in the talent and future of their prospect. So far, that faith looks justified.

The club and the player are in advanced talks over a new contract. The board understand that the midfielder, like winger Rio Ngumoha, is one of two gems with an enormous future who can put their names in the history of the club.

The good news for Nyoni is also that the opportunities he has received from Iraola can be seen more as a belief that he will be a starter for a long time than as a rotation strategy, merely offering a few minutes to a young reserve.

At Bournemouth, Iraola led a talented team of players under 23, with names such as Rayan and Eli Junior Kroupi, among others. He not only managed them, but developed the prospects, raising the talent of each one.

In a season in which Liverpool have many question marks and few answers, Nyoni looks a success. There is still plenty of room for improvement for the gem, but the future, and the present itself, are promising.

Genoa are on a very good run at the moment, having won four of their last five games, and have thus managed to bounce back from what was a tough start to the season. Just in time for the game against Milan, in other words, which is one of their biggest tests yet.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

With no European commitment, De Rossi’s side have been working on the training ground since the 2-1 win against Lecce last weekend. A different story compared to Milan, who faced Ferencvaros on Thursday evening and also lost that game.

Speaking to the media at his press conference yesterday, as transcribed by Calciomercato.com, De Rossi shared his thoughts on the game, Genoa’s current form and the quality of Milan’s team. He warned that they cannot afford to get too cocky.

“We had a little more time to prepare for the match, which is small advantage over Milan. We pushed a little harder, whereas last week we managed the load. We went a little deeper to analyse what we want to do and what we have done.”

#1827. Thomas Tuchel admits his relationship with Jude Bellingham is 'up and down' - but on the mend - as he reveals he's apologised to Kobbie Mainoo who is struggling at 'off a cliff' Man United

Published: 14:00 EST, 6 November 2026 | Updated: 15:27 EST, 6 November 2026

Thomas Tuchel says his rocky relationship with Jude Bellingham is on the mend after revealing he called his brother Jobe in to the England squad after some cajoling from the Real Madrid star.

Tuchel and Bellingham Snr have not always seen eye to eye during the German's time as England boss.

But Tuchel said today he hopes those days are behind him after he called 21-year-old Borussia Dortmund midfielder Jobe into this squad for next week's Nations League games against Croatia and Spain.

'It was a bit of an up and down [relationship] of course but we are in a good place,' said Tuchel.

'I love to be his coach. He's a top player, a very influential player and I think it goes both ways. If Jude was not feeling comfortable he would not perform on that level.

'In the moment you see he's happy to come into camp, he's happy with the role he has, he's fully invested and now to have the chance to have both of them is just the next step.

Thomas Tuchel has admitted he has an up and down relationship with Jude Bellingham

'I hope we have finished with the down. You never know as a coach!'

With injury to Bournemouth's Alex Scott and Arsenal's Myles Lewis-Skelly suspended for Thursday's Croatia game at Wembley, Tuchel sprung a surprise by elevating Jobe Bellingham from the Under 21s to the senior squad.

'Yeah Jude and I have spoken about his brother because I was aware it was always his dream to play with Jobe for England,' explained Tuchel.

'Jude was always saying: "Watch him, watch him he's good, he can make it". 'I would say: "Yeah we are watching him".

'I think he actually watched training very early in my reign. He came over and watched his brother train. We chatted and said it would be nice if one day he was with him.

'He was very kind and very polite and I'm glad to have him in camp. Everyone will compare them and he has to live with this.

Now Tuchel says he 'loves' to be Bellingham's coach after his brilliant World Cup campaign

Jude had a hand in brother Jobe being called up to the England squad for the first time

'They look similar, even in their movements, but they are very different players. Jobe is more defensive. I think they are also different characters, at least that's what I heard.

'He couldn't stop smiling when I called to tell him the news. He has the same beautiful smile like Jude so it's nice to have him.'

Tuchel's squad for what he insists are two important games was once again full of messages and insights into this thinking.

There was no room for Cole Palmer and Kobbie Mainoo after both players withdrew from the October campo with injuries. There was also no call up once again for Manchester City's Phil Foden.

Asked about Palmer, fit and ready now and in decent form at Chelsea, Tuchel said: 'It's not personal and we will never assume that he is not desperate to come and play.

'But the competition is on. It's about the ones who walk the walk and come to camp.

'Someone more intelligent once said to me: 'You cannot not communicate. You cannot not send a message.'

'So yeah. A nomination is always a message, yes.'

Tuchel revealed that he almost picked Foden – who hasn't played for England since March – after an upturn in his form but had second thoughts when he saw him relegated back to the bench at the Etihad Stadium.

'He is close and he will always be close,' said Tuchel.

'There were glimpses of the Phil Foden that we would love to see. He had these two matches with four or five goal involvements and assists and being so clinical.

Cole Palmer continues to be left out by Tuchel - while Phil Foden was close to a recall

'I got excited and thought: "That's it, that's, he found his mojo, he is getting back there". Then he dropped again and played again from the bench.

'I'm in love with him as a player. What is not to love?

'If you see the boy train it's just the highest, highest quality.

'But we're talking about numbers in an England shirt which are not in proportion to his talent and to his potential.

'If we can align this and become a regular City starter and be decisive, I think he has to be always an option.

'It was very close and it's also close for Eberechi Eze to keep his place with us. He's not starting for Arsenal.

'But the advantage was maybe that Morgan Gibbs-White and Eberechi Eze come again into camp. The advantage was that they have been in camp last time.'

Thomas Tuchel has told how he apologised in front of the whole England squad to Kobbie Mainoo for not giving him a single minute during the summer's World Cup in America.

Mainoo cut a lost and frustrated figure during England's campaign after a succession of players were picked ahead of him in his central midfield position.

The Manchester United star has not made Tuchel's squad for the forthcoming Nations League games with Croatia and Spain after withdrawing from the last camp with injury.

Tuchel revealed: 'He was hugely disappointed from the World Cup, and deservedly so.

'I said it in front of the team, in front of the staff.

'I said: "Sorry that I didn't pick you, you did nothing wrong, that is on me".

'He was disappointed and I think it cost him a bit of confidence.

Tuchel has noted how Man United 'fell off a cliff' - causing issues for Kobbie Mainoo

'He was excellent in training and in the way he presented himself through the tournament.

'So he was never a problem, the way he carried himself.

'Then he pulled out of last camp. I was desperate to give him the minutes. Desperate to include him in this new start, in the Nations League.

'But he then missed an excellent camp and also entered a difficult, difficult spell for himself.

'He was injured then Man United fell off a cliff a little bit performance-wise. So this is why he suffers from that.'

#1825. Champions League draw: Arsenal to renew Mourinho rivalry with Real Madrid tie

Arsenal will host old nemesis José Mourinho’s Real Madrid in the league phase of the Champions League.

Mourinho, the former Chelsea, Manchester United and Tottenham Hotspur manager, will return to London to resume hostilities against last season’s beaten finalists.

Other reunions from Thursday’s draw include Manchester City travelling to Barcelona, to whom they last week sold Rodri, and Liverpool visiting Inter Milan, who have signed Curtis Jones.

Arsenal will also travel to Harry Kane’s Bayern Munich, while United will host the Germans as well on their Champions League return in a repeat of the legendary 1999 final. Michael Carrick’s side will also visit Cesc Fàbregas’s Como.

Mourinho last managed at the Emirates Stadium in March 2021, barely a month before his sacking by Spurs.

During his two spells as Chelsea manager, Mourinho famously had run-ins with Arsenal’s Arsène Wenger.

Mourinho called Wenger a “specialist in failure” after the Frenchman failed to add to his three Premier League titles following his Portuguese counterpart’s arrival in London in 2004.

Last season, Mikel Arteta finally ended Arsenal’s long wait to be crowned champions of England but agonisingly missed out on European glory.

Verdict Premier League champions should not be daunted by any game, but Real Madrid – with Mourinho in control – has the feel of a defining match of the group stage. Facing Kane in Munich does not seem any easier. Some tough assignments here including a trip to Napoli but the pot-four teams seem straightforward for Mikel Arteta.

Verdict Playing against the European champions and travelling to Barcelona will be a true test of how much progress Enzo Maresca has made in the short time he has been at the Etihad Stadium. City’s other games do not look easy either but they should be defeating teams such as Sporting Lisbon and Porto – at least they would be expected to under Pep Guardiola.

Verdict The San Siro was where Arne Slot began to turn results around last season and Iraola getting a win there would be a big statement. Atlético staged a comeback at Anfield in 2020 and the repeat fixture will be tight. But there are enough winnable games there for Liverpool to reach the next round.

Verdict They will face a wall of noise in Istanbul when they play Galatasaray, but Villa will look to get points from the game. There are some tasty destinations for travelling fans and getting results there will ease the pressure on the match against PSG, who have been rattled by Villa before but remain a difficult opponent. The Nou Camp is a place where momentum can change in a season – for good or bad.

Verdict The repeat of the 1999 final is the standout fixture, but Michael Carrick should be looking beyond that match for the points needed to progress. He has been given a tough set of away games to navigate. They are winnable but difficult. So those games at Old Trafford will be very important.

That brings our coverage of the Champions League draw to an end, as the 36 teams found which eight teams they will be facing in the league phase of this season’s tournament. Thanks for joining us!

The league phase will kick off on 8 September and will be wrapped up after all teams play at the same time on 27 January.

The top eight teams of the league phase progress to the last 16 automatically, while teams that finish between ninth and 24th will be forced to navigate a play-off tie to reach the knockout stages.

So we have 144 fixtures decided but there are certainly a few heavyweight contests which stand out:

That brings the draw to an end! Just a reminder that the order of the fixtures is based on the pots and the respective home and away fixtures within the pots, rather than chronology.

That is pots two and three done. Just the pot four teams to sort out now, finding out which other pot four teams they will face.

Some crackers in there. Up next we will be finding out all the opponents for the pot two teams.

There is a fairly extensive video explanation of the format currently taking place. We should you be bringing you some fixtures very shortly...

The draw is now getting underway. Uefa deputy general secretary Giorgio Marchetti comes on stage to oversee proceedings. A reminder of the format:

The 36 teams will be split into four pots of nine, based on “club coefficient rankings”, with defending champions Paris St-Germain automatically named as the top seed.

Proceedings will begin with a team from pot one being drawn at random, and they will be allocated eight fixtures – four at home and four away – by an automated software. They will face two teams from each pot, with one home game and one away game per pot, while they cannot play a team from their country.

This will be done for all nine teams from pot one, before the same process takes place for pot two teams, though they will already know their pot one opponents. Pot three teams will then find out their pot three and four opponents, before the pot four sides are allocated their fixtures against each other.

But before the draw we will be hearing from Villa about the 2011 final, which he scored in as Barcelona dismantled Manchester United at Wembley.

He calls it a “great generation” of players, mentioning Lionel Messi, who also scored in the 3-1 win.

Henry will be part of the draw so he remains on stage as Ceferin departs. David Villa will also be coming onto the stage to help with proceedings. We are told the draw will be starting shortly.

We’re hearing from Henry now about losing the 2006 Champions League final with Arsenal and winning three years later with Barcelona.

He’s now discussing the current Arsenal crop and how they are getting closer to the trophy. He says if “they keep their core” and make some additions they can get over the line. But PSG “are an annoying team at the moment”.

Marquinhos on winning the respect award: “I’m very happy and honoured to be given this trophy. Fair play is an essential part of both football and daily life, and I will keep being respectful this year.”

Up next is the “Uefa President’s Award”? The winner is of course Thierry Henry and, fortunately, he is in attendance, so he’s up on the stage to collect this honour. A slow clap from Martin Keown in the crowd.

Reshmin Chowdhury and Pedro Pinto shuffle the musicians off the stage before outlining this evening’s itinerary.

Uefa president Aleksander Ceferin is then brought up to the stage, after a quiet summer, to announce Marquinhos as the winner of a new award, the Respect Beyond the Game award.

Marquinhos is not at the ceremony, so it will be PSG president Nasser Al-Khelaifi coming up to collect it. We hear from the defender on a video message.

The ceremony is underway in Monaco with a live performance of the famous anthem – orchestra and all – while pictures of previous winners play on the big screen in the background.

The 36 teams will be split into four pots of nine, based on “club coefficient rankings”, with defending champions Paris St-Germain automatically named as the top seed.

They will face two teams from each pot, with one home game and one away game per pot, while they cannot play a team from their country.

This will be done for all nine teams from pot one, before the same process takes place for pot two teams, though they will already know their pot one opponents. Pot three teams will then find out their pot three and four opponents, before the pot four sides are allocated their fixtures against each other.

There are five English teams involved in the Champions League this season – one short of the Premier League’s tally from last term.

Manchester City, Arsenal and Liverpool will be in pot one, while Manchester United and Aston Villa will be in pot two.

This evening’s ceremony should be getting underway in Monaco in a couple of minutes.

All set for this evening's #UCL draw in Monaco 📌🏆 pic.twitter.com/N3verDUO9y

Paris St-Germain will be aiming to become the first team to win three successive Champions Leagues since Real Madrid’s run of titles between 2016 and 2018.

The holders 🔴🔵#UCLdraw pic.twitter.com/eB05BNfWZi

This season is the third under the new format, with a league phase instead of a group stage, and Uefa has confirmed that fixtures that have taken place in the league phase of the two previous seasons cannot be repeated this time around.

For example, Liverpool cannot host Real Madrid in the league phase this term after welcoming the 15-time European champions to Anfield at this stage of the previous two campaigns. Andoni Iraola’s side could, however, travel to the Bernabeu for an away meeting with Madrid.

Similarly, Arsenal will not be travelling to San Siro to face Inter, but could host the Serie A champions at the Emirates.

Arsenal finished top of the league phase last season after winning all eight fixtures and it resulted in a favourable run to the final, facing Bayer Leverkusen, Sporting and Atletico Madrid.

Liverpool, meanwhile, topped the league phase in the 2024-25 campaign – the first season with the new format – but fell at the first hurdle in the knockout stages after being drawn against Paris St-Germain.

The Ligue 1 side have proven that it’s not essential to be firing the whole way through the tournament, finishing 15th and 11th in the league phase in the last two seasons but going on to lift the trophy on both occasions.

#1824. Premier League Team of the Week: Bruno Fernandes, Dominik Szoboszlai, Liam Delap

By Matt Law | 09 Nov 2026 10:01, Last updated: 09 Nov 2026 10:03

Arsenal sit five points clear at the top of the Premier League table heading into the November international break, with the Gunners beating Hull City 1-0 on Saturday afternoon.

Manchester City's domestic problems continued with a 3-1 loss at Nottingham Forest, while Chelsea suffered a shock 1-0 defeat to Sunderland at the Stadium of Light.

Brighton & Hove Albion and Liverpool were also victorious, but the most dramatic match of the weekend came at Old Trafford on Sunday afternoon, as Manchester United and Aston Villa played out a chaotic 4-4 draw.

Here, Sports Mole presents its Premier League Team of the Week for Gameweek 10 of the 2026-27 campaign, according to the data.

Tzolakis put in an excellent performance for Hull in the team's 1-0 defeat at Arsenal on Sunday; the goalkeeper made nine saves in total, and it would have been more comfortable for the Gunners had the 24-year-old not been in such impressive form.

Hume was a standout performer for Sunderland in their 1-0 win over Chelsea at the Stadium of Light; the 24-year-old won five aerial duels and made five tackles during a strong defensive performance against Xabi Alonso's side.

Vuskovic has been an exceptional signing for Brighton, and the 19-year-old was again excellent against Brentford, winning eight aerial duels and finishing with a pass success rate of 87%.

Cunha scored an excellent goal in Forest's win over Man City, while he also helped keep Erling Haaland quiet with a strong defensive performance in Saturday's late start.

Mykolenko set up Thierno Barry to score Everton's leveller against Coventry City on Friday, while he won six aerial duels and finished with a pass success rate of 84%.

Madueke was Arsenal's best performer in Saturday's 1-0 win over Hull, with the England international completing six dribbles and finishing with a pass success rate of 85%; the 24-year-old was the biggest threat for the Gunners on the afternoon.

A lifeline for Man Utd! ? Bruno Fernandes converts from the penalty spot to reduce the defecit! https://t.co/wy7L1iAhbx

Fernandes helped pull Man United back into the match against Villa on Sunday, scoring a penalty, while it was his corner that Patrick Dorgu headed in for 4-4 in the latter stages; this was much more like it from the Red Devils captain.

Gross has been one of the top performers in the Premier League this season, and the 35-year-old was again excellent against Brentford, finding the back of the net from the penalty spot, in addition to finishing with a pass success rate of 87%.

Szoboszlai was back to his best for Liverpool against Palace on Sunday, setting up Alexis Mac Allister to make it 1-0 to the Reds late in the first period, and he was a dominant force for the Merseyside outfit in the middle of the pitch.

"The day that Delap ARRIVES" ? Nottingham Forest regain their two-goal lead! https://t.co/5yk5eIhPhe

Delap scored twice in Forest's 3-1 win over Man City on Saturday, and both goals were of a high standard; the 23-year-old has found it tough since a summer move to Forest, but he showed his quality with an excellent performance against the Citizens.

Thierno Barry has bagged his second goal in four minutes to put Everton ahead! ? https://t.co/8F5dYhSbLS

Barry has now scored 10 times in 13 appearances for Everton this season courtesy of his brace against Coventry on Friday evening, while the 24-year-old also set up Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall for Everton's third of the match on home soil.

Premier League Team of the Week (4-4-2): Tzolakis; Hume, Vuskovic, Cunha, Mykolenko; Madueke, Fernandes, Gross, Szoboszlai; Delap, Barry

#1823. AC Milan Women 0-3 Inter: Chances squandered and a silly red card

Milan Women failed to replicate the heroics of the men’s team in the Derby della Madonnina, conceding three goals against Inter after a silly red card.

After the odd-goal defeat to Como last night time out, Milan Women were out for revenge this afternoon, and perhaps also a little inspired by the men’s win in the derby last weekend. However, Suzanne Bakker’s side made life very difficult for themselves.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

In the first half, Milan actually had a couple of good opportunities to take the lead and make it a very different game. After just four minutes, the veteran Christy Grimshaw got a good chance in the box, but failed to connect with the cross from the left with her head from close range.

About ten minutes later, Mawa Sesay picked up on a loose ball after a mistake by Inter’s backline. However, she somehow missed the target and didn’t even force the goalkeeper to a save, effectively squandering a 1v1 by rushing the shot.

In the second half, the game remained fairly even but one moment proved costly for Milan. As Benedetta Glionna made her way into the box, the aforementioned Grimshaw made her evening worse with a little kick, resulting in a penalty for the away side (somewhat cheap, but fair).

Haley Bugeja made no mistakes from the spot, firing a great shot straight down the middle to give her side the lead in the 57th minute. Milan then began their pursuit of an equaliser after that but instead of a goal, around five minutes later, Sandra Ogalla was sent off.

The goalkeeper used her hands a little bit too early, touching the ball outside the penalty box, and the referee immediately spotted it. Bakker made use of the VAR challenge, prompting the referee to have a look at the screen, but the decision was upheld. A silly red card indeed.

Deputy goalkeeper Sally Rainey was brought on but just a few minutes later, Inter doubled their lead through Glionna. It was a well-worked move, in fairness, but the defending could have been better at the far post. That was in the 67th minute.

Milan tried to get back into the game but struggled with only ten players. And so, in the 83rd minute, Inter were awarded another penalty. This one was even cheaper than the first, as Angelica Soffia barely touched the player.

Despite another VAR check, the decision was upheld and Bugeja bagged her second of the night. That concluded the night from a goalscoring point of view, and Milan Women suffered their second consecutive defeat.
